Maya — thanks for the clear notes and the attachment. High level, we can meet the SLOs you called out but will want to validate with a short perf pilot (48–72h sustained run) that exercises real traffic shapes. Below is the recommended ops + cost levers and immediate asks from your infra team.

Summary of recommended levers (prioritized):
- Continuous batching: enable request coalescing at the gateway for non-interactive workflows; target batch windows of 8–16 tokens for suggestions. This reduces per-token compute by ~20–35% for batched workloads.
- Prefix/KV caching: cache common prefixes (search/product titles) at the edge and at the model runtime for streaming flows to reduce repeated KV cache populating. Expect latency drop on warm prefixes (p95 improvement) and significant cost reduction for hot items.
- Quantization profiles: start pilot on a mixed path — use 4-bit PTQ for lower-cost paths (redwood-4b-q4) and 8-bit/INT8 for critical queries (redwood-13b-int8). We recommend the following mapping: suggestions -> redwood-4b-q4, checkout assistant -> redwood-13b-int8.
- Model variants + routing: soft routing by policy (latency-sensitive -> smaller, lower-latency quantized variant; quality-sensitive -> larger variant). Auto-fallback to a cheaper variant on sustained queueing.
- Autoscaling + concurrency shaping: set target concurrency per worker to 32 streams for streaming models, with burst workers up to 128 streams during promos.
- Streaming chunk config: use 64–128 token chunk flush for streaming to balance latency vs tokenization overhead.

Operational pre-reqs (what we need from Horizon):
- VPC peering + subnet ranges + egress IP allowlist (for pilot nodes)
- A short-lived API key and a test dataset (sample 2k requests with streaming flags) for the perf run
- Expected traffic shape (per-second timeline) and a list of top 500 queries to warm caches
- SLA/retention asks (any audit/logging requirements) so we can enable full tracing if required

Immediate next steps / owners:
- Marcus (me): schedule perf pilot with SE and infra; propose pilot window Wed-Fri this week
- Ben Carter (cc): I'll hand to Ben for model-mapping + runtime tuning; Ben will share a pilot config and estimated cost envelope by EOD today
- Maya / Horizon: share VPC info and sample traffic by EOD tomorrow

I attached a short pilot MAP (Horizon-Pilot-MAP.xlsx) with the proposed config and a draft timeline.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if any of this needs faster alignment.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi all — Ben here (SE). I took Marcus's notes and sketched the pilot runtime config and an initial cost estimate. Below are concrete knobs we will change during the run and what to measure.

Pilot runtime config (baseline):
- Models: redwood-13b-int8 for interactive checkout assistant, redwood-4b-q4 for suggestions
- Node type: A2-standard-like GPUs with NVLink; 12 workers per pool
- Concurrency per worker: streaming=32, non-streaming=64; queue timeout 250ms
- Batching: dynamic batching with 10ms coalescing window for non-streaming; continuous batching heuristics enabled
- Cache warmup: preload top-500 prefixes at start of pilot

Measurement plan (to validate SLOs and cost):
- Latency breakdown: gateway, network, model-infer p50/p95/p99; token-level breakdown where possible
- Cost estimate: tokens consumed, GPU-seconds, avg concurrency, predicted monthly cost under three traffic profiles (pilot, scaled-typical, promo peak)
- Quality checks: side-by-side diffs on 200 golden prompts between model variants; automated regression alert if BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drops >2%

Estimated cost (pilot window 72h):
- Compute-only: ~$1,100 (pilot-sized pool)
- Including telemetry/ingress: ~$1,350
- Projected monthly at pilot config (steady): ~$6,500/mo; with aggressive 4b-only routing for suggestions we can approach your target ~$4k/mo but expect ~6–8% quality delta on rare long-tail queries.

Tradeoffs and recommendations:
- If Horizon wants to strongly favor latency at p99, prefer smaller quantized variants and increase warm-worker count (higher fixed cost).
- If Horizon wants to strongly favor cost, we can expand routing to redwood-4b-q4 for a larger fraction of traffic and apply heavier prefix caching.
- For streaming p50 sub-70ms: we will tune chunk flush to 64 tokens and ensure KV cache hits for the most common prefixes; this is the most sensitive lever.

I can push the pilot config to the shared Drive and a short bash script to run the perf harness. Marcus — if you want, I’ll schedule the perf run for Thu-Fri and loop in infra.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
